analysis: The closest option develops close reading, comparative narratives and stylistics alongside a sustained sequence in Western art, connected Renaissance art, African heritage, modern museums and histories of art interpretation. Historical inquiry, sociology and qualitative methods support its broader cultural and institutional analysis.

The power option uses gender history, empire, sociology, social movements, political philosophy and institutions to study identity, power and representation. Media and Race, media and environment, and heritage make the links to cultural expression explicit. Comparative and EU politics supply institutional grounding. They are complementary rather than direct matches for UvA literary methods.

The screen and communication option shares literature and media foundations with the first option. It uses rhetoric, public persuasion, archaeology, environmental media and philosophy in place of art history and broader social and historical research. Adaptation, documentary, poetry and performance give it a distinct organizing focus. All three schedules are feasible and pairwise above the distinctness threshold.

Rechecked alignment against what courses teach. Literary Meaning overlaps in critical frameworks with Literary and Cultural Theory Today; moving image study overlaps in visual representation; historical art and material media remain supporting UCR study. UvA maintains a denser sequence of literary-cultural research, a workshop and a required independent thesis.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce close reading, literary interpretation and foundational concepts for analysing texts and culture.
Both analyse moving images and representation. UCR introduces film form and media history. UvA focuses on mobility and the affective and political force of images.
Both use close analysis to explain how form creates meaning. UCR concentrates on language and style. UvA works across texts, images and objects.
Both take a comparative global approach to literary traditions and their cultural meanings.
Both mobilise theory through focused cultural case studies; UCR centres race and ethnicity in media.
Both analyse narrative construction across media; UCR focuses specifically on adaptation from text to film.

Both use literary and cultural theories to interpret texts. UCR applies perspectives such as Marxism, feminism and psychoanalysis to literary meaning. UvA covers a wider range of contemporary critical approaches.
Both examine relations among culture, media, technology and environmental or material questions.
Both engage advanced contemporary theory and debate; UCR approaches these debates through social theory and civil society.
Both provide philosophical foundations for humanities interpretation; UCR surveys historical philosophical traditions rather than philosophy of the humanities as a field.
